text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 7 in history:
1307 - King Edward I of England died on his way north to subdue a rebellion in Scotland; he was was succeeded by Edward II.
1572 - Sigismund II Augustus, the last Jagiellon of Poland, died; during his reign he united Livonia and the duchy of Lithuania with Poland.
1573 - Giacomo da Vignola, Italian architect and writer on architecture, died.
1752 - Joseph Marie Jacquard, French inventor of the Jacquard loom, born.
1807 - The first of the Treaties of Tilsit was signed, under which France and Russia became allies and divided Europe between them.
1816 - Richard Brinsley Butler Sheridan, Irish playwright, died. His best known works were "School for Scandal" and "The Critic"; he later became a politician and noted parliamentary orator.
1846 - Commodore J.D. Sloat of the U.S. Navy raised the American flag in Monterey, proclaiming U.S. citizenship for California.
1854 - Georg Simon Ohm, German physicist, died; the physical unit measuring electrical resistance was named after him.
1864 - Gustav Mahler, Austrian composer of nine symphonies and the famous "Das Lied von der Erde", born.
1887 - Marc Chagall, Russian painter, printmaker and designer, born.
1889 - George Cukor, U.S. film director, born. Of the 50 films he directed, the most notable were "Dinner at Eight", "Little Women", "The Philadelphia Story" and "A Star is Born".
1911 - Gian Carlo Menotti, Italian composer, born. Among his works are the operas "The Consul" and "The Medium". He was also founder of the Festival of Two Worlds at Spoleto.
1930 - Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, English author and creator of "Sherlock Holmes", died.
1937 - Following the setting up of a commission to investigate the mandate in Palestine, the Peel Report was published in Britain. It recommended that there should be separate Arab and Jewish states.
1940 - Ringo Starr, drummer in the Beatles pop group, born.
1941 - President Roosevelt announced that U.S. forces had landed in Iceland to prevent a Nazi invasion.
1952 - The liner United States made the fastest-ever crossing of the Atlantic, on her maiden voyage.
1978 - The Solomon Islands gained independence from Britain.
1981 - President Reagan nominated Sandra Day O'Connor to become a Supreme Court justice; she became the first woman member of the Supreme Court in September.
1984 - Dame Flora Robson, notable English stage and screen actress, died; best remembered for such roles as Queen Elizabeth I in "Fire Over England" in 1931.
1991 - A republic movement backed by more than 100 prominent Australians was formally launched.
1994 - Northern Yemeni forces gained total control of their southern foe's last bastion, Aden, crushing a bid to recreate an independent state; fleeing southern leaders vowed to continue the war.
1995 - Flamboyant Italian ex-foreign minister Gianni De Michelis was sentenced to four years in prison for corruption.
1996 - Rightist Christian Democrat Jaime Nebot conceded defeat in Ecuador's runoff presidential election to populist Abdala Bucaram of the center-left Roldosista Party.
